findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Basis.lean:157 and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Adjugate.lean:333 use `RingHom.mapMatrix_apply`; `eq_intCast` is Mathlib/Data/Int/Cast/Lemmas.lean:336. Rubric: `show` without a documenting comment, and reliance on defeq across a wrapper/coercion.
findings.fix: Use the explicit lemmas: `rw [← RingHom.mapMatrix_apply, ← RingHom.map_det, eq_intCast]` (or `Int.coe_castRingHom`) instead of the `show ... from rfl` and the trailing `rfl`.
findings.issue: `hmap` is proved by `rw [show (N.map (Int.cast : ℤ → k)) = (Int.castRingHom k).mapMatrix N from rfl, ← RingHom.map_det]` followed by a bare `rfl`. Both steps rest on undocumented defeq: the first unfolds the bundled `RingHom.mapMatrix` wrapper plus the `FunLike` coercion, the second identifies `((N.det : ℤ) : k)` with `(Int.castRingHom k) N.det`. No comment justifies either.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Basis.lean:257-262 `Module.Basis.invertibleToMatrix (b b' : Basis ι R₂ M₂) : Invertible (b.toMatrix b')`; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NonsingularInverse.lean:137 `Matrix.isUnit_det_of_invertible`.
findings.fix: Derive it from `Module.Basis.invertibleToMatrix B B'` and `Matrix.isUnit_det_of_invertible (B.toMatrix ⇑B')`, then rewrite by `htoMatrix`, `Matrix.det_transpose`, `← hmap` and conclude with `IsUnit.ne_zero`; this drops the named-lemma chain and the by-contradiction step.
findings.issue: `hdet` rebuilds "a change-of-basis matrix has nonzero determinant" by hand: `congrArg Matrix.det (B.toMatrix_mul_toMatrix_flip B')`, then a chain of `det_mul`/`det_one`/`det_transpose` and a proof by contradiction ending in `zero_ne_one`. Mathlib already has this fact as an instance.

findings.evidence: Spanning.lean:253-256 vs Artin.lean:212-214 are the same set literal; `hmem` (Artin.lean:215-217) is `Iff.rfl`, which only typechecks because the two literals coincide.
findings.fix: In Spanning.lean add a named generating set (e.g. `inducedCharactersSet k G 𝒮`) with `inducedCharactersFrom k G 𝒮 = Submodule.span k (inducedCharactersSet k G 𝒮)` and a `mem_inducedCharactersSet` characterization, as was already done for `cyclicInducedCharacters_eq_inducedCharactersFrom`; then Artin.lean gets `hspan` by rewriting `cyclicInducedCharacters_eq_top` rather than by duplicating the set and re-deriving spanning.
findings.issue: The local set `𝒢` (lines 212-214) re-spells, character for character, the generating set inside `inducedCharactersFrom` (Spanning.lean:254-256), and `hspan` (218-222) then rebuilds `Submodule.span k 𝒢 = ⊤` from `cyclicInducedCharacters_eq_top` through a term-mode `▸` chain. The duplication exists only because Spanning.lean never names its generating set; the two copies must be kept in sync by hand.

findings.evidence: Artin.lean:228 defines `T := fun i => (e i : ClassFunction k G)`; line 232 asserts it equals `Subtype.val ∘ e` by `rfl`. Rubric: flag any `show`/`change` used without a comment documenting why the goal cannot be reached otherwise.
findings.fix: Introduce the equality as `have hT : ⇑T = Subtype.val ∘ e := funext fun _ => rfl` with a one-line comment, or define `T := Subtype.val ∘ e` directly so no defeq step is needed.
findings.issue: `rw [show T = Subtype.val ∘ e from rfl, ...]` closes the step by an undocumented definitional equality (eta-expansion of the `let`-bound `T`), with no comment saying why a lemma is unavailable — the same smell as line 115.

summary: The lattice-descent proof in Artin.lean twice closes goals by undocumented definitional equality (`show ... from rfl` across `RingHom.mapMatrix`/`Subtype.val ∘ e`) where explicit Mathlib lemmas exist, hand-rolls the standard "change-of-basis determinant is nonzero" fact instead of using `Module.Basis.invertibleToMatrix`, and re-spells the generating set of `inducedCharactersFrom` verbatim because Spanning.lean never exposes it.
